::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 22nd 1861  
**From:** Otterbourne,Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, C0171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Miss Wilford](people/person_1520.qmd)

Yesterday was the [Ampfield](organizations/other_124.qmd) anniversary of the consecration of the Church and I took a grand holiday - including a walk from Ampfield to Hursley with [Mr Keble](people/person_798.qmd), and so I could not write but we have read your Seven Campbells and like them very much. I suspect boys would believe in them more if John Lackland always went by his English name.

I do not think a Scottish minister stands on the same ground as an English dissenter, as their Calvinism is hereditary and certainly not indifferent to its creed (I don’t mean that all dissenters are) I fancy the all denominations was a free expression of [Mrs Blackburn](people/person_159.qmd), who is herself a Churchwoman. But reading the story, I thought it would better fit [Miss Mozley](people/person_1061.qmd)’s [Magazine for the Young](organizations/other_79.qmd) and if you like I would send it to her. She is a very clever far seeing person and I always think her criticisms worth more than anyone’s that I know. Do you know I think [Groombridge](organizations/other_148.qmd)[^1] must have refused it because it would have been so ridiculous to have had one story about a doctor with 7 daughters and another about a doctor with 7 sons. I should rather like to see you start with some other publisher than [Masters](people/person_981.qmd), for he does publish so many silly stories that they rather swamp the wiser ones by making one mistrust his name. I would have nothing to do with the [Guild of St Alban](organizations/other_24.qmd) if I were you. I think there is much more use in insinuating sound doctrine and opinions into periodicals read by all the world than in writing in those that belong to a small section of a party like this, and especially when one is never quite sure what they will say next. I cannot say I have - more than yourself - made up my mind whether [Garibaldi](people/person_1855.qmd) and Co ought to be favoured with my good opinion. I suppose no one will know for the next 100 years when [it has all become history](organizations/other_149.qmd). I believe your spelling of Photineé is quite right, I had it sent to me in a list of Corfiote names spelt with a long Greek <u>e</u>.[^2] Many thanks for your kind invitation to see the wonders of Woolwich. I do not see much chance of our going to London for some time to come, but our doings of that kind usually come to pass in a hurry. Pray remember us to [Mrs Cristall](people/person_384.qmd). I am glad to know she is with you, that we may not in vain assail the river of dust that lies between us and [St Cross](organizations/other_130.qmd). I am relieved to hear that you do not kill Lambert - it is much more moral to live than die only there are cases when in stories people have to die to improve their families & I expected this to be one. Let me know if you like me to try the Mag for the Young

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

[^1]: From the 1840s on, Groombridge and Sons, Paternoster Row, London published a similar range of books to the Mozleys, religious, children’s stories, natural history and so on. CMY contributed to their *Magnet Stories for Summer Days and Winter Nights* 8 vols (London, Groombridge 1860-5), which were collections of children’s stories by various authors.
[^2]: CMY was collecting material for her *History of Christian Names*
